description: Test-only lexicon. Identical in shape to the shipped lexicon, but every refusal is ADVISORY rather than BLOCKING, which exercises the path where unresolved language travels WITH a draft instead of stopping it. Not a ruling on any term; see docs/AMBIGUITY-POLICY.md for the real rulings.

window.description: Test fixture: the sentence the match sits in, plus the one after it.

resolution_needed.description_template: Test fixture: state whether "{phrase}" uses the ruled basis or {qualifier_phrases}.

basis_qualifier_policy.limits: Test fixture: declared surface patterns inside a declared window, nothing more.

attachment.rule: A declared qualifier re-bases a ruled term ONLY when it is syntactically attached to the ruled measurement — modifying the term itself, or standing as the term's own comparative complement, or glossing the term's own word. A qualifier that merely co-occurs in the window attaches to something else in the sentence and is NOT a re-basing. This is a deliberate choice of PRECISION over RECALL, and the reason it is safe is that it is not the only thing telling the truth: every resolution this guard permits still carries source_basis_agreement NOT_VERIFIED, which declines to certify that the source agrees with the ruled basis. A guard that fired on every co-occurrence would refuse ordinary trading prose — an ATR stop, a bar-count expiry, a moving-average trend filter — and refusing a valid strategy is a defect, not caution. See docs/AMBIGUITY-POLICY.md, 'What attaches a qualifier to a ruled term'.

forms.description: The qualifier overlaps the term's own modifier slot: the basis_slot group each PARAMETERISE pattern declares, which is the run of words the pattern allows between its ruled adjective and its ruled head noun. Words sitting in that slot modify the measurement itself, so any category attaches there — "a large ATR wick", "a large recent wick", "a larger than average wick". This form is why a hit INSIDE a term's matched span must be examined rather than discarded: the slot is a wildcard, and a re-basing lands in it.

A COMPARATIVE qualifier begins immediately after the term match, with nothing between them but complement_filler. A comparative is the connective that binds a yardstick to a measurement, which is what makes it attach: "a large wick RELATIVE TO the recent average". Non-comparative qualifiers never attach this way, because a bare yardstick noun after the term attaches to whatever else the clause is about — "a large wick above the 200 period moving average" places the wick, it does not measure it. Once a comparative has attached, qualifiers of any category lying between it and the end of its sentence name the displacing basis and are reported with it.

The source restates the term's own ruled word and then defines it: "a large wick, and by large I mean twice the 14-period ATR". What attaches the gloss is that it NAMES one of the words the term itself matched — gloss_constructions carry an {anchor} placeholder which is replaced, per match, by the ruled words that match actually consumed. Qualifiers lying between the gloss and the end of its sentence are the basis the gloss states. A gloss naming no declared qualifier re-bases nothing. This is the only form that reaches past the term's own sentence, and how far it reaches is window.sentences_after.

gloss_constructions.reason: the source names the ruled word and then says what it means by it
the source defines the ruled word outright
the source defines or measures the ruled word as something

attachment.not_attached: Deliberately NOT treated as re-basing, because each attaches to something other than the ruled measurement: a stop or target sized in ATR ("a large wick. My stop is 2 ATR below entry."); a bar-count expiry or persistence window, which PID line 136 REQUIRES a package to state ("the setup expires within 3 bars", "expires after 4 bars"); a trend or location filter naming an average ("a large wick above the 200 period moving average"); a reference to prior bars used as a price level rather than a yardstick ("a large wick that clears the previous bars' high"). These resolve, and source_basis_agreement stays NOT_VERIFIED.
